# Copilot Instructions

## Project Overview
- A physically-based ray tracer with parallel CPU and GPU (OptiX) implementations, built up from "Ray Tracing in One Weekend"/"The Next Week"/"The Rest of Your Life" into a pbrt-v4-style feature set: 65 scenes (ids 0-64), a wide material/BxDF library, multiple light and camera types, real triangle-mesh + texture support, BVH acceleration, volumetrics, and an SPPM (photon-mapping) integrator alongside standard path tracing. See README.md for the full feature list and Known Limitations for what's still incomplete (GPU SPPM is scene-11-only, BDPT/MLT are tested libraries not wired into the CLI, hair has no literal fiber geometry, etc.) — don't assume everything mentioned in code comments is fully wired up; check.
- Active production code lives in `src/TheRestOfYourLife/` (CPU scenes/materials/lights) and `src/shared/` (CPU+GPU shared headers: BxDFs, cameras, lights, sampling — many are `CPU_GPU`-tagged templates compiled by both the host compiler and nvcc).
- **The unified launcher entry point is `main.cpp` at the repo root**, not `launcher/main.cpp` — that file used to exist but was empty/dead since the project's first commit and has been deleted. `launcher/launcher.vcxproj` references `..\main.cpp`. GPU is the default render mode (`--gpu`); `--cpu` and `--sppm` are opt-in flags.
- The CPU renderer is a static library project named `cpu_renderer` (formerly `raytracing_book`). It builds `cpu_renderer.lib`, linked into the launcher via a ProjectReference, called in-process through `cpu_render_main()` (`cpu_renderer/cpu_interface.h`).
- The GPU renderer uses OptiX 9.1 and is built as a static library project named `optix_renderer`, building `optix_renderer.lib`, called in-process through `optix_render_main()` (`gpu/optix/optix_interface.h`). Three GPU backends exist: the default recursive mega-kernel (`gpu/optix/optix_programs.cu`), an opt-in wavefront/queue-based path tracer (`gpu/optix/wavefront_*`, enabled via `RAY_TRACER_WAVEFRONT=1` env var, not a CLI flag), and GPU SPPM (`gpu/optix/sppm_*`, `--sppm --gpu`, scene 11 only).
- Build environment: CUDA compilation requires Visual Studio Developer Command Prompt/PowerShell (vcvars64.bat). Regular PowerShell causes nvcc/cudafe++ access violations.
- **GPU hardware**: developed against an RTX 5080 (Blackwell, SM 12.0), driver 595.79+, OptiX 9.1, CUDA 13.2+.

## Build System Gotcha: PTX/obj staleness across output directories
- The optix_renderer project's custom MSBuild targets copy freshly-built PTX (`optix_programs.ptx`, `wavefront_programs.ptx`, `sppm_programs.ptx`) to `RayTracer_Package/` automatically, but **not reliably to `bin/Release/` or `x64/Release/`** (the test binary's own output directories) — this has caused real, reproducible-looking GPU test failures ("invalid program counter" CUDA errors) that were actually just stale PTX, not code bugs. If you touch any header shared between host code and device `.cu` files (e.g. a struct in `optix_types.h`), **touch all the `.cu` files** (`optix_programs.cu`, `wavefront_*.cu`, `sppm_*.cu`) to force MSBuild to recompile their PTX/obj, then verify with `md5sum` that `gpu/optix/*.ptx`, `bin/Release/*.ptx`, `x64/Release/*.ptx`, and `RayTracer_Package/*.ptx` all match before trusting a GPU test run.
- Even after confirming PTX consistency, the full test suite (~2,850 tests, all in one process) shows genuine non-deterministic GPU-resource-pressure flakiness under `--gtest_shuffle` with different seeds — a handful of GPU tests near the end of a long run can fail even when the code is correct. Don't chase this as a code bug without first re-running with shuffled order/seeds to check reproducibility.

## Qt GUI Application
- The Qt-based GUI is located in `qt_gui/` and built using Qt 6.11.1 with MinGW 64-bit.
- The GUI executable is `RayTracerGUI.exe` and is deployed to the `RayTracer_Package/` directory.
- The GUI spawns the console launcher `ray_tracer.exe` as a subprocess to perform rendering. Scene metadata (description, GPU compatibility, perf hint) is loaded live from a separate `scene_metadata.dll` (built from `scene_metadata.vcxproj`), not hardcoded in the GUI — **this DLL must be rebuilt whenever `scene_registry.h` changes**, or the GUI will show a stale scene list. `RayTracerGUI.exe` holds a lock on this DLL while running, so it needs to be closed before rebuilding.
- **Deployment**: MSBuild automatically deploys `ray_tracer.exe` and the OptiX PTX files to `RayTracer_Package/` via post-build events when you build the launcher or optix_renderer projects. No manual copying needed for those two, but see the PTX staleness gotcha above for `bin/`/`x64/` test-binary directories.
- **Verification**: Run `.\scripts\deploy_launcher.ps1` to verify deployment succeeded after building.
- **Qt dependencies**: Run `windeployqt.exe RayTracerGUI.exe --no-translations` in the `RayTracer_Package` directory to deploy Qt6 DLLs if missing.

## Rendering Guidelines
- Scene definitions live in `src/TheRestOfYourLife/scene_registry.h` (CPU) and `gpu/optix/scene_builder.cpp` (GPU, one `build_X_gpu()` function + dispatch case per scene) — keep both in sync when adding a scene; there is no single shared scene-description format.
- The GPU path tracer's recursive backend uses naive path tracing while the CPU uses importance sampling (PDF-based, NEE + MIS). Older code/comments may still say the GPU "requires ~100x more samples" from an earlier, less-MIS-complete GPU implementation — verify against current `shade_material()` (`optix_device_helpers.h`) rather than trusting that number blindly.
- Set the ray-origin offset appropriately (historically 0.01f for 555-unit Cornell box scenes) to prevent self-intersection; use a minimum t-value of 0.001f for sphere intersections instead of 0.0f.
- Mesh scenes (37-64) load external `.obj` files from `models/`, searched via a climbing relative-path convention (tries `models/`, `../models/`, `../../models/`, ... up to 5-6 levels) so a single asset copy works regardless of the render's current working directory (`RayTracer_Package/`, `bin/Release/`, a test binary's own cwd, ...). The three largest meshes (Sponza, Bistro, Rungholt) and their texture directories are tracked via **Git LFS** — `git lfs pull` if they show up as small pointer files instead of real assets.

## File Handling Guidelines
- Visual Studio holds exclusive write locks on open .cpp files. An editor tool that writes to Visual Studio's in-memory buffer (visible in the editor) does NOT flush to disk while Visual Studio has the file open.
- PowerShell's `Set-Content` will fail with "file being used by another process."
- Workaround: Create a new file instead of editing a file that is currently open in the IDE, or verify on-disk content before trusting tool-view edits.
- **CRLF discipline**: C++ source files in this repo are CRLF-only. Verify with `perl -ne 'print if /\r(?!\n)|(?<!\r)\n/' <file> | wc -l` expecting 0 after any edit. For large multi-line insertions, writing a standalone script (Python/PowerShell) that reads, edits, and writes back with explicit `\r\n` handling is more reliable than an in-place text edit tool for avoiding line-ending mismatches. Data files (README.md, .gitattributes, etc.) are not held to this convention — check the existing file's own line endings before assuming.

## Terminal Guidelines
- Always read terminal output promptly rather than waiting long durations for terminal commands.
